items.text: GraphicsDeviceManager reshapes the preferred back buffer on iOS and Android (Portrait gives width = the smaller edge; any other DisplayOrientation, including the default, gives the landscape shape) and forwards SupportedOrientations to the window only there. No test exercises that phone branch: DefaultBackBufferPreferencesAreTheXnaDefaults covers the desktop verbatim size and skips itself when the platform name is iOS or Android, and the iOS simulator lane only launches a one-frame smoke app.

The native Linux controller-mapping reader (community gamecontrollerdb format, loaded from CNA_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG_FILE / CNA_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG by the X11 and Wayland evdev hub) is tested only on hand-written entries in CI. The one test against a real database file, LinuxEvdevMapping.EveryEntryOfADatabaseFileIsRead, skips unless CNA_TEST_GAMECONTROLLERDB names a file, and no workflow sets that variable; mapped-pad behaviour with physical generic HID pads has no recorded evidence.
items.evidence: modules/platform/tests/CNA/Platform/LinuxEvdevMappingTests.cpp (EveryEntryOfADatabaseFileIsRead, GTEST_SKIP); modules/platform/src/Linux/EvdevMapping.cpp (ControllerMappingDatabase::FromEnvironment); grep of .github/workflows for CNA_TEST_GAMECONTROLLERDB (no hit)

items.text: StorageDevice::DeviceChanged is declared as a static event but nothing in the snapshot raises it. The genuine XNA 4.0 Storage assembly subscribes the event's raiser to FrameworkCallbackLinker.StorageDeviceChanged, so XNA raises it when a storage device changes; CNA has no source for such a change on its desktop storage root.
